scope: LINK/FEC real fragmenter / FastBlockEncoder 20:20 / BlockDecoder / LINK reassembler, no TLS/TUN/netem/product benchmark

inputs.drop_pattern: Drop every systematic fragment of first logical datagram and an equal number of parity shards of each FEC block containing its fragments. Different wire orders but equal count/size-class erasure budget, no random sample.

hypothesis: Faster 8ms partial parity closure can reduce per-size-class FEC block size for 12ms sparse large LINK datagrams. Equal 20% erasures can be unrecoverable for early one-message blocks while longer 100ms grouping has independent redundancy equations; this is POSSIBLE MECHANISM, not established cause of real netem 5205.
next: If short/long test passes, decide minimum policy preserving lowRTT sparse and Normal1 5205; do not silently change FEC coding policy. Need core/race and all protectors before claiming gain.
